newsitem.title: GREECE: Nat. Bank of Greece ponders $150-200mln bond loan.
newsitem.headline: Nat. Bank of Greece ponders $150-200mln bond loan.

text.p: The National Bank of Greece wants to issue a $150 to $200 million subordinated bond loan in the international markets in the first four months of 1997, its chairman Theodore Karatzas told a news conference.
"The management is also considering the issuance of a $150 to $200 million subordinated bond loan, tier two capital...the first ever by a Greek credit institution," said Karatzas.
The revaluation of fixed assets on December 31, 1996 boosted the bank's equity capital by 14.2 billion drachmas, he said.

The share capital of the National Bank also increased by 102 billion drachmas in 1996 when the Finance Ministry and the bank agreed to replace a maturing convertible bond with a new one, tier one capital, said Karatzas.
The chairman of Greece's largest commercial bank said the National Bank would raise its share capital in 1997 but the timing and magnitude of the increase would be announced later.
Karatzas added the bank would invest more than an estimated six billion drachmas annually in the next few years to upgrade its technological know-how while containing its operating costs.
The bank will choose a unified platform for all its systems, including online, in 1997 and pick a strategic advisor in the first two months for designing an integrated information system.
It has completed a tender for the acquisition of an integrated system to monitor and manage market risks.
The operating costs of the bank increased 11.5 percent in 1996 from 17.3 percent in 1995, he said.
Karatzas pointed out that the National Bank wrote off bad loans of 54 billion drachmas in 1996 and equity participations of 63.6 billion drachmas in a bid to polish its balance sheet.
He said the bank would do everything in its power to have the drachma traded on a 24-hour basis worldwide.

The National Bank chairman announced that the Athens dealing room will be open until 1900 (1800 GMT) and the London dealing room until 2000 (1900 GMT) starting February 3 quoting bid and offer prices for all drachma products.

"The 1997 goal is to extend this capability to America so that the dealing rooms of Atlantic Bank and Canada quote prices until 1700 New York time," he said. -- Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
